title: Satellite manufacturing thrives in California despite cost and regulatory pressures
summary: Muon Space opened a new satellite manufacturing facility in San Jose, California, with support from state, local, and military representatives. Despite economic and regulatory challenges, the satellite manufacturing sector in California continues to grow.

title: Think tank warns Europe’s orbital compute gap is widening
summary: A European think tank warns that Europe is falling behind in orbital computing infrastructure, risking dependency on foreign, particularly U.S. and Chinese, space-based data centers. The European Space Policy Institute highlights the widening gap in this critical technology sector.

title: Neuraspace raises $18 million to expand sovereign space awareness
summary: Neuraspace, a Portuguese space traffic management startup, raised $18 million to enhance European space domain awareness and defense capabilities. The funding will support the expansion of sovereign space awareness initiatives.

title: Voyager seeks relaxed requirements in NASA commercial space station RFP
summary: Voyager Technologies is optimistic about its Starlab commercial space station but requests adjustments to NASA's requirements in the commercial space station Request for Proposal (RFP). The company seeks relaxed criteria to better support Starlab's development.

title: SpaceX to begin Starship orbital flights
summary: SpaceX is set to begin orbital flights of its Starship vehicle, with plans to deploy upgraded Starlink satellites on its next mission as early as this month.

title: Rocket Lab, STR win Space Force contracts for airborne-target tracking
summary: Rocket Lab and Sierra Technical Services (STR) secured $615 million in Space Force contracts for the AMTI satellite program to track airborne targets. The contracts were awarded alongside a third unnamed vendor.

title: Telesat lands $1.63 billion Canadian defense contract
summary: Telesat secured a $1.63 billion Canadian defense contract to expand its Lightspeed LEO network, increasing the planned constellation to 225 spacecraft.

title: NOAA purchases Spire hyperspectral microwave sounder data
summary: NOAA extended a $3 million contract with Spire Global to evaluate data from its Hyperspectral Microwave Sounder (HyMS). The agreement aims to assess the satellite data's utility for weather forecasting and climate research.

title: Rubicon ASCENT thruster moves from hot-fire testing to production
summary: Rubicon Space Systems has completed hot-fire testing of its Velox 5-newton ASCENT monopropellant thruster, transitioning it to production. The thruster is expected to support on-orbit operations by 2027.

title: Military demand shapes market for satellite propulsion
summary: Military demand is driving investment in satellite propulsion systems, enabling small satellites to change orbits more freely. Startups and established manufacturers are focusing on developing these engines.
company: Military (implied demand), Startups and established spacecraft manufacturers (general)

title: Mars dust is toxic. How will future astronauts deal with it?
summary: Mars dust contains carcinogens like silica and heavy metals, posing health risks to future astronauts. Mitigation strategies are being explored to protect human explorers.

title: 'The Ninth Jedi' review: This anime spin-off abandons 'Star Wars' canon, and it's all the stronger for it
summary: The anime spin-off 'The Ninth Jedi' from Star Wars: Visions abandons traditional Star Wars canon, offering a fresh take that the franchise reportedly needed. The series is praised for its unique approach despite not being part of the main Star Wars continuity.

title: Heading to Europe or the U.K. for the Aug. 12 solar eclipse? Best eclipse glasses to buy before you leave — or after you arrive
summary: The news provides recommendations for purchasing solar eclipse glasses for viewing the Aug. 12 solar eclipse in Europe or the U.K. It highlights safe viewing options for observers in those regions.

title: Total solar eclipse Aug. 12, 2026 live updates — 1 week to go
summary: The news covers live updates on the total solar eclipse occurring on August 12, 2026, with one week remaining until the event. Live reports will be broadcasted from Greenland and Spain.

title: SpaceX wants to launch next Starship this month (and catch it, too), Elon Musk says in 1st earnings call since historic IPO
summary: SpaceX aims to launch its next Starship rocket this month, with plans to attempt catching it during the flight. This follows Elon Musk's announcement in the company's first earnings call since its historic IPO.

title: SpaceX launches 3 giant BlueBird direct-to-cell satellites on Falcon 9 rocket (video)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched three large BlueBird direct-to-cell satellites for AST SpaceMobile using a Falcon 9 rocket. The mission took place early on August 5.

title: When a total solar eclipse darkens the sky on Aug. 12, these citizen scientists will be watching
summary: A citizen scientist initiative will observe the total solar eclipse on Aug. 12 to engage the public. The project aims to bring people closer to the celestial event.

title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites on 90th Falcon 9 flight of the year (video)
summary: SpaceX launched 24 Starlink satellites aboard a Falcon 9 rocket, marking the 90th orbital mission of the year. This flight continues the rapid deployment of SpaceX's broadband constellation.

title: APOD: 2026 August 5 – Spokes on Saturn’s B Ring
summary: APOD features an image of Saturn's B Ring with spokes, scheduled for August 5, 2026. This is part of the Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) series showcasing cosmic phenomena.

title: The Paradox of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park
summary: The Paradox of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park describes a coastal dune field in Brazil that resembles a desert but annually fills with freshwater lagoons. This unique natural phenomenon combines arid-like sand dunes with seasonal rainwater pools.

title: NASA Will Attempt to Observe Rocket Part’s Lunar Impact
summary: NASA and SpaceX are tracking a Falcon 9 upper stage expected to impact the Moon on August 5. The event will be observed using ground-based and space-based telescopes to collect lunar data.

title: NASA’s PUNCH Sharpens Solar Storm Forecasting in First Test
summary: NASA’s PUNCH mission accurately predicted the arrival of a solar eruption within 30 minutes in its first test. The results, presented at a scientific meeting, could significantly improve solar storm forecasting.

title: Ames Science Stars of the Month – August 2026
summary: NASA Ames Science Directorate recognized Danielle Lopez, Jennifer Claudio, and Duncan Mifsud as Science Stars of the Month for August 2026 for their contributions to the NASA mission. Their work highlights the entrepreneurial spirit, technical expertise, and collaboration essential for space exploration.

title: August 2026 Satellite Puzzler
summary: The August 2026 Satellite Puzzler challenges participants to identify the location of a satellite image and explain its significance. This event engages the public in satellite imagery analysis and highlights advancements in Earth observation technology.

title: NASA Provides Updates on Moon Base Cargo Landers, Tech Demonstrations
summary: NASA is advancing its Moon Base plans with commercial partners like Blue Origin and Firefly Aerospace to deliver cargo landers by 2028. The outpost near the Moon’s South Pole will support science, technology, and future human missions.

title: Roman Space Telescope Plaque Install
summary: Technicians installed a commemorative plaque on NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, honoring Dr. Nancy Grace Roman, NASA’s first chief astronomer. The plaque includes a memory card with over 1.3 million entries.

title: APOD: 2026 August 4 – Curious Cometary Knots in the Helix Nebula
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) features an image of curious cometary knots in the Helix Nebula, showcasing a stunning astronomical phenomenon. The post is part of APOD's daily series highlighting fascinating cosmic images with explanations by professional astronomers.

title: Crew-13 pilot reflects on career, training, and upcoming science ahead of flight to ISS
summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the next International Space Station mission, Crew-13, with the pilot reflecting on their career, training, and upcoming scientific research. The mission is part of ongoing efforts to advance space science and human spaceflight.

title: While SpaceX recovers Ship 40, Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14
summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean. Meanwhile, Ship 41 is being prepared for testing ahead of Flight 14.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first week of August is expected to be busy with multiple launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The manifest highlights a significant activity in the space industry.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the ISS in 2026, following ongoing redesign efforts. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted the progress in addressing previous technical issues.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has conducted two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase while retrofitting efforts continue on Pad 1. The transition to Block 3 flights marks a new phase in SpaceX's launch operations.

title: Blue Origin continues rebuilding LC-36, prepares testing alternatives for New Glenn second stage
summary: Blue Origin is continuing the rebuilding of Launch Complex 36 (LC-36) and exploring alternative testing methods for the second stage of its New Glenn rocket following a recent pad explosion during a static fire test.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: Ship 40 successfully completed its mission and returned intact during SpaceX's Starship Flight 13. This achievement paves the way for potential in-flight catch attempts in future missions.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket launch in China and a Falcon 9 mission.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io after two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the moon's volcanic activity and geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn for its upcoming missions.

title: TEC Business to Business website
summary: TEC Business to Business website provides industry news related to the space sector. The source covers various aspects of the space industry, including launches, satellites, and technology.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) released a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over its 50-year history. The publication celebrates the agency's milestones and contributions to space exploration.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESA's ESTEC technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's disk, effectively playing hide and seek with Earth. The mission aims to provide unprecedented views of the solar atmosphere.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase startups with innovative space ideas on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands. The event aims to facilitate collaboration and explore opportunities within Europe's space industry.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: Next-generation antennas are being enhanced with advanced silicon-based components. These innovations are expected to improve communication and data transmission capabilities in space applications.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber at ESTEC, confirming its electronics are space-ready. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A brand new green chemical propulsion lab has conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to present the follow-up to the CM25 meeting, detailing planned activities, priorities, and industrial opportunities. These events aim to facilitate direct exchange between ESA and the industrial community.

title: SpaceX Reports Q2 Earnings
summary: SpaceX released its Q2 earnings, beating expectations after its record-breaking June IPO. The company's first quarterly results were highlighted in a recent report.

title: Neuraspace Raises €15.6M to Scale its SDA Service
summary: Neuraspace has secured €15.6 million in funding to expand its Space Domain Awareness (SDA) services. The company aims to address growing challenges as satellite deployments and defense needs in space increase.

title: FL Governor Candidate Launches Space Race Policy
summary: A Florida gubernatorial candidate has proposed a space race policy to attract launches, investments, and high-paying jobs to the state. The initiative aims to compete with other states and countries for space industry opportunities.

title: Xona Clears Final Regulatory Hurdle for PNT Constellation
summary: Xona Space Systems has received FCC approval to broadcast Pulsar navigation signals from a full satellite constellation, marking the final regulatory hurdle before scaling deployment.

title: Kreios Taps Kongsberg NanoAvionics for 2028 VLEO Demo
summary: Kreios has selected Kongsberg NanoAvionics for a 2028 Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) demonstration mission to test its ABEP thruster at various altitudes below Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The mission aims to validate Kreios' propulsion capabilities in this challenging orbital regime.

title: True Anomaly Chases an Evading Target
summary: True Anomaly successfully executed the first in-space pursuit of an evading target as part of the VICTUS HAZE mission. This milestone marks a significant advancement in space maneuvering and satellite operations.

title: AFRL Adds $11.7M to Blue Origin’s Point-to-Point Cargo Contract
summary: The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) added $11.7 million to Blue Origin's contract to study point-to-point cargo delivery using its launcher. This funding aims to explore the potential of Blue Origin's technology for rapid global logistics.

title: K2 Space Raises $500M Series D at $6.8B Valuation
summary: K2 Space secured a $500 million Series D funding round, valuing the company at $6.8 billion. This brings K2 Space's total financing to over $1 billion since 2022.

title: NordSpace Funds NVD Amid Canada’s Export Push
summary: NordSpace Ventures invested in North Vector Dynamics, a company developing sovereign missile capabilities. This aligns with Canada's push to enhance domestic defense exports.

title: Report: Our Launch Cadence Forecast For Next-Gen Rockets
summary: The article discusses the expected flight cadence ramp for next-gen reusable rockets such as New Glenn, Neutron, Nova, Terran R, and Eclipse. It aims to forecast the launch frequency of these advanced rockets.

title: L3Harris Confirms Successful Deployment for First Perimeter Truss Reflector on ViaSat-3
summary: L3Harris Technologies announced the successful deployment of its first perimeter truss reflector on the ViaSat-3 Flight 3 satellite, which was launched by SpaceX in late April. This marks the third deployment in ViaSat's satellite constellation.

title: Kreios Space to Demo Air-breathing Electric Propulsion in VLEO With NanoAvionics
summary: Kreios Space will demonstrate an air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) system in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) using a spacecraft bus provided by Kongsberg NanoAvionics. This marks a significant step for air-breathing propulsion technology in space.

title: Telesat Expands Lightspeed Constellation for Arctic Military Satcom Program
summary: Telesat secured a $1.9 billion contract with the Canadian government to expand its Lightspeed constellation by 69 satellites for Arctic military satcom connectivity. This expansion will enhance secure communications in the Arctic region.

title: Endeavor Optical Networks Emerges From Stealth to Build Optical MEO Data Transfer
summary: Endeavor Optical Networks has emerged from stealth to develop an optical satellite network in Medium-Earth Orbit (MEO) for space-based data transfer. The startup aims to leverage MEO for enhanced data transmission capabilities.

title: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space to Build SpainSat NG-III
summary: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space have been contracted by Hisdesat to build the SpainSat NG-III secure satellite communications satellite for Spain. Airbus, as the prime contractor, announced the award on July 31.

title: ETL Acquires Software Developer Amphinicy Technologies
summary: ETL Systems has acquired Amphinicy Technologies, a software developer specializing in satcom and Earth Observation markets. The acquisition aims to enhance ETL's ability to address complex ground segment challenges.

title: Xona Gets Approval to Deploy Commercial Navigation Constellation
summary: Xona has received FCC approval to deploy its commercial navigation constellation called Pulsar, which plans to include more than 250 satellites. The company announced the authorization to broadcast radionavigation signals.

title: Hughes Files for Chapter 11 With Plan to Reorganize Around Enterprise, Defense Business
summary: Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection to reorganize its operations around enterprise, government, and defense customers due to a decline in consumer demand.

title: AccelerCom and Eclipse Space Reveals Details of D2D Collaboration
summary: AccelerComm has completed two engineering engagements with Eclipse Space to define the physical-layer architecture for its next-generation Direct-to-Device spacecraft. The collaboration highlights advancements in sovereign satellite infrastructure.

title: K2 Space Secures Series D Funding After Hitting $1 Billion Contract Value Milestone
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in Series D funding, valuing the company at nearly $7 billion. This follows the achievement of a $1 billion contract value milestone.
